body.p: Claims 1-20 are pending in the application. By this Response, claims 1-4, 6 and 19-20 have been amended. No new matter is added by these amendments, which are supported by the Applicant's specification as filed, e.g. paragraphs [00198], [00206], [00255]-[00257] and [00265]. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims in view of the remarks presented below.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Liu et al.

("Tracking Vital Signs During Sleep Leveraging Off-the-shelf WiFi"; hereinafter "Liu"), in view of Xu et al. ("Attention-based Walking Gait and Direction Recognition in Wi-Fi Networks"; hereinafter "Xu"), and further in view of Li et al. (CN 109684941; hereinafter "Li").
Applicant respectfully traverses each of the above rejections, and does not agree on any Official Notice taken in the Office Action.
Without agreeing on the above rejections and solely for expediting the allowance of the application, independent claim 1 is amended to recite among other things:
obtaining a time series of channel information (CI) of the wireless channel based
on the received wireless signal,
computing a time series of denoised CI (DCI) by denoising the time series of
CI (TSCI),
computing a time series of concatenated CI (TSCCI) based on a
concatenation of the TSCI and the time series of DCI (TSDCI), each concatenated
CI (CCI) being computed by concatenating a respective CI and a respective DCI
corresponding to the CI,
computing a one dimensional (1D) characteristic function of CCI of the TSCCI in
a sliding time window,
computing a two dimensional (2D) decomposition of the TSCCI based on the 1D
characteristic function in the sliding time window,
enhancing the 2D decomposition based on a non-separable vertical highpass
horizontal lowpass filtering, and
monitoring the periodic motion of the vital sign based on the enhanced 2D
decomposition. (Emphasis added.)

The Office Action correctly noted that Liu does not disclose "computing a time series of denoised CI (DCI) by denoising the time series of CI (TSCI)," and "computing a concatenation of the TSCI and the time series of DCI (TSDCI)," as previously recited in claim 1. The Office Action then relied on Xu to teach these features. See, Office Action, pp. 3-4. Without agreeing to such teachings, Applicant respectfully submits that Xu does not teach or suggest: "computing a time series of concatenated CI (TSCCI) based on a concatenation of the TSCI and the time series of DCI (TSDCI), each concatenated CI (CCI) being computed by concatenating a respective CI and a respective DCI corresponding to the CI," as recited in the amended claim
1. (Emphasis added.)

Xu mentioned 3 steps of "Raw CSI Processing" in Section IV-B. See, Xu, pp. 5-6. In step B1 ("Long Delay Removal"), Xu transformed the original CSI from CFR to CIR using IFFT, removed CIR components with long propagation delays, and then convert the CIR back to CFR using FFT. See, Xu, p. 5. After step B1, Xu performed step B2 ("CSI Denoising"), by applying a Butterworth bandpass filter followed by weighted moving average to denoise the CSI. See, Xu, pp. 5-6. After step B2, Xu performed step B3 ("CSI Refining"), by performing principal component analysis (PCA) to obtain the "PCA components" such as "first PCA component" and "first three principal components." See, Xu, p. 6.

Then Xu mentioned 3 steps of "Walking Profile Generation" in Section IV-C. See, Xu, pp. 6-7. In step C1 ("Walking Detection"), "the Energy of Interest (EI), which equals the sum of (normalized) magnitudes squared of FFT coefficients in the frequency range 20-60 Hz, is calculated to detect walking movement." See, Xu, p. 6. When walking movement is detected, Xu performed step C2 and step C3. In step C2 ("Spectrogram Generation"), Xu converted "the

time-domain refined CSI data sequence to the spectrogram" and computed "spectrogram (of the 1st PCA component)." See, Xu, pp. 6-7. Then in step C3 ("Profile Splicing"), Xu "keeps the data of 64 out of the 85 FFT points in the spectrogram, which corresponds to the frequency range of around 10-70Hz, and stacks the data of each PCA component to form the primary walking profile with dimensions for each PCA component..." See, Xu, p. 7.

Even if the stacking in Xu can imply concatenation, which Applicant does not concede, Xu did NOT stack the TSCI and TSDCI directly. Instead, Xu "stacked" several "PCA components" computed from denoised CSI in steps B2 and B3. That is, the original CSI (or alleged TSCI) in Xu is used as input in step B1 and but is never used again in steps B2, B3, C1, C2 and C3. As such, Xu does NOT teach or suggest concatenation of TSCI and TSDCI, such that "each concatenated CI (CCI) being computed by concatenating a respective CI and a respective DCI corresponding to the CI," as recited in the amended claim 1. (Emphasis added.)

In addition, the Office Action correctly noted that Liu does not disclose "enhancing the 2D decomposition based on a vertical highpass filtering and a horizontal lowpass filtering," as previously recited in claim 1. The Office Action then relied on Li to teach these features. See, Office Action, pp. 3-4. Without agreeing to such teachings, Applicant respectfully submits that Li does not teach or suggest: "enhancing the 2D decomposition based on a non-separable vertical highpass horizontal lowpass filtering," as recited in the amended claim 1. (Emphasis added.) The filters used in Li are separable filters. It is non-obvious to one with ordinary skill in the art to modify Li to enhance the 2D decomposition based on a non-separable vertical highpass horizontal lowpass filtering.

It is well settled that establishing a prima facie case of obviousness requires that all claim limitations recited in a claim must be taught or suggested by the prior art. MPEP §2143.03. Clearly, taken individually or in combination, the cited references do not pass this test. Thus, a prima facie case of obviousness cannot be established with respect to claim 1. Thus, claim 1 is patentable.
Claims 2-18 depend from claim 1, and are thus likewise patentable for at least the same reasons as discussed above with respect to claim 1, and for the additional features recited therein.

Independent claims 19-20 have amended to include similar features as claim 1, and are thus likewise patentable for at least the same reasons as discussed above with respect to claim 1, and for the additional features recited therein.
In view of the above amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that all rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103 are overcome and should be withdrawn.
No Disclaimers or Disavowals

Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are not patentable over the cited references. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application. Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that capture any subject matter supported by the present disclosure, including subject matter found to be specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution. Accordingly, reviewers of this or any parent, child or related prosecution history shall not
reasonably infer that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the present application.

In view of the above, each of the presently pending claims in this application is believed to be in immediate condition for allowance. Accordingly, the Examiner is respectfully requested to withdraw the outstanding rejection of the claims and to pass this application to issue.
